Joint Bandwidth and Regularization Tuning for LHWPR

tune.lhwpr.Rd

Select LHWPR bandwidth and regularization parameters with cross-validation or Gaussian information criteria.

Usage

tune.lhwpr(
  formula,
  data,
  Z,
  bw_grid = NULL,
  family = c("gaussian", "binomial"),
  penalty = c("lasso", "mcp", "scad"),
  alpha_grid = 1,
  gamma_grid = NULL,
  lambda = NULL,
  nlambda = 100L,
  lambda_min_ratio = NULL,
  penalty_factor = NULL,
  case_weights = NULL,
  standardize = TRUE,
  kernel = hgwr_kernel_names(),
  adaptive = TRUE,
  bandwidth_type = c("knn", "volume"),
  geometry = c("lorentz", "tangent"),
  tangent_ref = NULL,
  dMat = NULL,
  engine = c("dense", "knn"),
  resampling = c("kfold", "loo", "blocked"),
  nfolds = 5L,
  fold_id = NULL,
  rule = c("min", "1se", "sparse_1se"),
  control = lhwpr_control(),
  refit = TRUE,
  bw_lower = NULL,
  bw_upper = NULL,
  n_bw = 15L,
  criterion = c(
    "cv", "aicc", "aic", "bic", "gcv", "ebic", "ebic_refit"
  ),
  ebic_gamma = 0.5,
  refine = NULL,
  n_refine = 7L,
  refine_alpha = FALSE,
  expand_bounds = TRUE,
  compare_lhwr = TRUE,
  eligibility_kkt_tol = 1e-05
)

# S3 method for class 'tune.lhwpr'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

formula, data, Z

Model formula, analysis data, and Lorentz coordinates.

bw_grid

Positive candidate bandwidths. When NULL, an adaptive kNN grid is generated automatically.

bw_lower, bw_upper

Optional lower and upper adaptive-kNN bounds used only when bw_grid = NULL.

n_bw

Number of automatically generated adaptive-kNN candidates.

family, penalty

Response family and structural penalty.

alpha_grid

Candidate alpha values.

gamma_grid

Optional MCP or SCAD gamma values.

lambda

Optional common decreasing absolute lambda path.

nlambda, lambda_min_ratio

Automatic lambda-path controls.

penalty_factor, case_weights, standardize

Penalized preprocessing controls; see lhwpr().

kernel, adaptive, bandwidth_type, geometry, tangent_ref, dMat, engine

Locality and geometry controls; see lhwpr().

resampling

Leave-one-out, K-fold, or blocked validation.

nfolds

Number of automatically constructed deterministic K-folds.

fold_id

Optional fold identifier per observation; required for blocked validation. Without this argument, K-fold allocation cycles through input row order deterministically; it is not randomly shuffled. Supply a frozen random or scientifically defined blocked assignment when that is intended.

rule

Minimum-score, one-standard-error, or sparse-one-standard-error selection. The latter two require criterion = "cv".

control

A value returned by lhwpr_control().

refit

Whether to fit the selected model on all observations.

criterion

Selection score. Cross-validation is the default. Gaussian models additionally support AIC, AICc, BIC, GCV, path-based EBIC, and the refit-based "ebic_refit" sensitivity criterion.

ebic_gamma

EBIC model-space penalty in \([0,1]\).

refine

Whether to refine the bandwidth grid around the provisional optimum. NULL refines automatic grids and leaves supplied grids unchanged.

n_refine

Number of candidates in the local bandwidth refinement.

refine_alpha

Whether to evaluate alpha midpoints adjacent to the provisionally selected alpha.

expand_bounds

Whether an automatic lower search boundary may expand toward its model-dimension safety limit. User-supplied bounds are respected.

compare_lhwr

Whether to evaluate an unpenalized LHWR reference using the same folds and bandwidths.

eligibility_kkt_tol

Maximum recorded KKT violation allowed for an eligible tuning row. All relevant focal fits must also converge; CV requires both validation and full-data path fits to pass.

x

A tune.lhwpr object.

...

Unused additional arguments.

Details

Tuning is conditional on the supplied representation and prepared design. Predictor standardization, the representation, and its tangent reference are prepared once for the supplied sample, not relearned within each fold. To evaluate an entire learned pipeline after tuning, use an outer validation workflow with transformations and representations fitted on the outer training sample and applied unchanged to validation observations.

Within each bandwidth and alpha configuration, all validation fits use one common absolute lambda path. For K-fold and blocked validation, its upper end is the maximum KKT threshold across folds. The "1se" rule chooses the most regularized eligible model, breaking ties toward a larger bandwidth. The "sparse_1se" rule first minimizes the number of selected coefficient surfaces within the same one-standard-error set.

All selection rules use the same numerical eligibility mask. A candidate must have complete convergence and a maximum recorded KKT violation no larger than eligibility_kkt_tol; Gaussian criteria retain their additional effective degrees-of-freedom restrictions. The final fit reuses the exact decreasing lambda prefix evaluated for the selected configuration instead of solving the selected lambda in isolation. The returned selected_lambda_path and refit_diagnostics record this path and its convergence/KKT certificate.

When bw_grid = NULL, automatic selection is available for adaptive kNN bandwidths. The lower bound is model-dimension aware and at least 20 neighbors; the default upper bound is \(n-1\). A cached coarse search is followed by a local refinement. If a default lower boundary is provisionally selected, the search may expand downward but never below the model-dimension safety limit. The returned object records and plots boundary solutions. Supply an explicit bw_grid for fixed-radius or volume bandwidths.

For Gaussian paths, ridge uses the exact smoother trace. Lasso and elastic net use a conditional active-set smoother, while MCP and SCAD additionally use their local piecewise penalty curvature. Here \(n\) is the number of positive-case-weight observations. If \(\nu\) denotes the effective parameter count including the Gaussian scale parameter and \(L\) is minus twice the maximized Gaussian log likelihood, the reported criteria include $$\mathrm{AIC}=L+2\nu,$$ $$\mathrm{AICc}=\mathrm{AIC}+ 2\nu(\nu+1)/(n-\nu-1),$$ $$\mathrm{BIC}=L+\log(n)\nu.$$ GCV divides the weighted residual mean square by the squared remaining smoother fraction, giving \((\mathrm{RSS}/n)/(1-\mathrm{tr}(S)/n)^2\), where \(S\) is the conditional fitted smoother and \(\mathrm{RSS}\) is the residual sum of squares under the normalized case weights described below. Gaussian path-information criteria can select only rows with edf_valid = TRUE; refit EBIC additionally requires post_edf_valid = TRUE.

The primary EBIC augments the pathwise BIC with a model-space term. In this expression \(\gamma\) is ebic_gamma, not the MCP/SCAD concavity parameter, and \(p_{search}\) counts predictors with positive penalty factors. The active-surface count \(q_{surface}\) is defined below: $$\mathrm{EBIC}=\mathrm{BIC}_{path}+ 2\gamma\log {p_{search} \choose q_{surface}}.$$ The optional criterion = "ebic_refit" sensitivity score replaces \(\mathrm{BIC}_{path}\) with the BIC from an unpenalized local refit on each selected active set. Refit scores with at most one residual degree of freedom are recorded as infinite and cannot be selected; post_residual_df and post_edf_valid retain this diagnostic. Here \(q_{surface}\) is the integer count of penalized coefficient surfaces whose standardized coefficient magnitude exceeds \(10^{-10}\) at one or more focal locations. Predictors with zero penalty factors contribute to smoother complexity but not to the model-space term. The selection table stores its logarithmic model-space term in ebic_model_space_log and flags a nonempty full-surface model, for which this term is zero, in ebic_model_space_zero. Case weights are normalized to sum to the number of positive-weight observations when computing Gaussian likelihood criteria. These are path-selection diagnostics, not post-selection coefficient standard errors. Binomial tuning currently requires criterion = "cv".

Value

A "tune.lhwpr" object containing the complete selection table, information criteria, numerical eligibility and support summaries, fold scores, search history, boundary diagnostics, the same-fold LHWR reference, selected row and exact lambda prefix, fold identifiers, and optionally the certified full-data refit.

Examples

set.seed(2)
H <- simulate_H2(35, r_max = 2)
dat <- data.frame(y = rnorm(35), x = rnorm(35))
selection <- tune.lhwpr(
  y ~ x,
  data = dat,
  Z = H$Z,
  bw_lower = 12,
  bw_upper = 28,
  n_bw = 5,
  nlambda = 5,
  nfolds = 3,
  criterion = "cv",
  rule = "sparse_1se"
)
selection
